overview: Superintendent Dr. Suzanne B. Galusi discussed the educational vision and space requirements for a proposed new Medford High School building in an interview on Medford Happenings. The conversation detailed the physical limitations of the existing facility, planned curriculum integrations, and capital design choices ahead of a June 10 building concept decision.

items.title: Educational Outcomes and Student Belonging
items.summary: Superintendent Galusi outlined Medford's K-12 instructional vision, which aims to replicate the collaborative and identity-affirming learning environments of vocational shops in standard academic classrooms.

items.title: Existing Facility Design Constraints
items.summary: Galusi explained that the current high school building isolates academic, arts, and vocational programs from one another and contains classrooms, vocational shops, and public areas that fail to meet state size guidelines and ADA accessibility standards.

items.title: Flexible Layouts and Future Adaptation
items.summary: Galusi described how a new facility will integrate flexible, multi-purpose communal spaces and STEM maker areas to accommodate shifting educational needs over the next several decades.

items.title: Building Design Concepts and Spatial Adjacency
items.summary: Galusi discussed the five design concepts under review by the school building committee and emphasized that the selected layout must resolve teacher classroom-sharing issues and optimize programmatic adjacencies.

items.title: Capital Cost Reductions and Space Prioritization
items.summary: Galusi detailed a space reduction strategy that proposes cutting office and duplicate auxiliary shop spaces to ensure student classrooms and essential community-facing services remain intact.

items.title: Taxpayer Value Proposition and the Cost of Inaction
items.summary: Galusi highlighted the mounting maintenance costs and structural failures of the existing building, arguing that failure to rebuild would restrict educational quality and jeopardize critical community support systems like the Medford Family Network.
